summary: Collective-intelligence surveys — answering a named set of ideas someone is asked to choose between: the ideas chosen in priority order, plus one new idea that was not in the set. Most requests are someone recording their answer to a set that already exists.
in_scope: Answering a survey someone has been given — recording a person's or an agent's response to a set of ideas that already exists, which is the ordinary request
Recording which ideas someone chose from a named survey's set, and the priority order they put them in
Contributing one new idea that was not already in the set, alongside a selection or on its own
Reading the set of ideas a response is chosen from out of a JSON or CSV dataset over HTTP, with `ideas fetch "<url>"`, at the moment the program compiles
Bounding how many ideas a response may select, via min-choices and max-choices, and refusing at compile time any response that breaks those bounds
Keeping the originating dataset's own ids on the ideas, so a selection means something back where the set came from
Group ideation and brainstorming where the point is which ideas a person favours and in what order
Being written and edited as code by a person in the editor or by an AI agent through update_item, both producing the identical record
out_of_scope: Assessment and quiz items — multiple choice with a right answer, hot text, cloze, matching, ordering, short answer, essays and rubrics. L0182 gathers opinions and does NOT score anyone; use L0180 for graded questions, and never route an assessment request here.
Scoring, marking, answer keys, correctness and points. A survey response is never right or wrong, so L0182 has no notion of a correct answer — a request for one belongs to L0180.
Conventional questionnaires and forms — demographics, Likert scales, satisfaction ratings, contact forms, sign-up flows and branching questionnaire logic are not built yet.

A survey-taking flow. L0182 does NOT describe screens, steps, navigation or submission, and there is no interactive player: it never walks anyone through anything, and the rendered view only displays the record. A flow would be a different language or a different client.
Drawing the sample. `fetch` reads whatever list the dataset serves, whole and in order — L0182 does NOT hold a pool, does NOT sample or shuffle it, and never re-reads it once a program has compiled.
Aggregating across respondents. L0182 records ONE response and does NOT compute a group ranking, tally, score or live result of any kind; ranking many responses together is not built yet.
Running the statistics — significance testing, clustering, sentiment analysis or any analysis of the responses collected.
Recruiting, quotas, screening, incentives and panel management.
Enforcing one response per person. A program holds a single response and does NOT authenticate anyone, so nothing here prevents the same person answering twice.
Images, audio and video as the objects being chosen between — an idea is a line of text.
